question: Which method registers a service with a scoped lifetime, and how long does a scoped service live in an MVC app?
expected_answer: Use AddScoped. A scoped service lives for a single request in an MVC or Razor Pages app (for a Blazor app, the lifetime of the circuit).
evidence: AddScoped method registers the service with a scoped lifetime

question: How do I register a service so a new instance is created per HTTP request?
expected_answer: Register it with AddScoped. A scoped lifetime is a single request in an MVC or Razor Pages app.
evidence: AddScoped method registers the service with a scoped lifetime

question: My custom middleware throws a runtime exception when I inject a scoped service into its constructor. What should I do instead?
expected_answer: Constructor injection forces the scoped service to behave like a singleton. Inject the service into the middleware's Invoke or InvokeAsync method instead, or use factory-based middleware, which is activated per request.
evidence: Using constructor injection throws a runtime exception

question: How do I register and resolve keyed services?
expected_answer: Register them with a key using AddKeyedSingleton, AddKeyedScoped or AddKeyedTransient, and resolve a specific one with the [FromKeyedServices("key")] attribute.
evidence: AddKeyedSingleton

question: In what order does ASP.NET Core middleware run?
expected_answer: Middleware runs in the order it is added in the Program file for the request, and in the reverse order for the response.
evidence: defines the order in which middleware are invoked on a request

question: How can a middleware stop a request from reaching the rest of the pipeline?
expected_answer: By not invoking the next middleware, which short-circuits the pipeline. A middleware that short-circuits is called terminal middleware.
evidence: short-circuiting the pipeline

question: What is the difference between IOptions, IOptionsSnapshot and IOptionsMonitor?
expected_answer: IOptions is a singleton that doesn't read configuration changes after startup or support named options. IOptionsSnapshot is scoped, is recomputed on every request and supports named options, so it can't be injected into a singleton. IOptionsMonitor retrieves current options and supports change notifications.
evidence: Is registered as a scoped service, so it can't be injected into a singleton service

question: I changed appsettings.json while my app was running, but my IOptions<T> values didn't update. Why?
expected_answer: IOptions doesn't read configuration changes made after the app has started. Use IOptionsSnapshot (or IOptionsMonitor) to read updated values.
evidence: To read changes after the app has started

question: Which environment does ASP.NET Core use if no environment variable is set?
expected_answer: Production. If neither DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT nor ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT is set, Production is the default environment.
evidence: environment is the default environment

question: Where are static files stored by default, and which call enables serving them?
expected_answer: In the web root, {CONTENT ROOT}/wwwroot by default. Static file handling is enabled by calling MapStaticAssets.
evidence: To enable static file handling in ASP.NET Core, call MapStaticAssets

question: How do I configure a custom error page for the Production environment?
expected_answer: Call UseExceptionHandler. The middleware catches and logs unhandled exceptions and re-executes the request in an alternate pipeline using the specified path.
evidence: To configure a custom error handling page for the `Production` environment, call UseExceptionHandler

question: How do I run a long-running task in the background of my web app?
expected_answer: Implement a hosted service, typically by deriving from BackgroundService (a base class for a long-running IHostedService) and overriding ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken).
evidence: BackgroundService is a base class for implementing a long running IHostedService

question: Why shouldn't I manage HttpClient lifetimes myself, and what should I use instead?
expected_answer: Use IHttpClientFactory. It manages the pooling and lifetime of the underlying handlers, which avoids common DNS problems that occur when HttpClient lifetimes are managed manually.
evidence: Automatic management avoids common DNS

question: Which route constraint makes a route parameter match only integers?
expected_answer: The int constraint, for example {id:int}.
evidence: {id:int}

question: Which URL does Kestrel listen on if no endpoints are configured?
expected_answer: http://localhost:5000.
evidence: If there's no endpoint configuration, Kestrel binds to the `http://localhost:5000` URL

question: What does the @key directive attribute do in Blazor?
expected_answer: It retains the relationship between elements or components and model objects when a rendered list changes, so Blazor preserves the right elements or components instead of reusing them in the wrong place.
evidence: to retain element, component, and model relationships

question: In what order are OnInitialized and OnParametersSet called when a component first renders?
expected_answer: OnInitialized{Async} is called first, then OnParametersSet{Async}. In each pair the synchronous method is called before the asynchronous one.
evidence: Call `OnParametersSet{Async}`

question: What is the firstRender parameter of OnAfterRender used for?
expected_answer: It is true the first time the component instance is rendered, so it can be used to make sure initialization work runs only once.
evidence: Is set to `true` the first time that the component instance is rendered

question: Why does my Blazor component's initialization code run twice?
expected_answer: Because of prerendering: the component renders twice, once for prerendering and once when setting up interactivity.
evidence: must render twice: once for prerendering and once for setting up interactivity

question: How do I apply a render mode to a Razor component?
expected_answer: Use the @rendermode directive on the component instance or on the component definition. The modes are Static Server, Interactive Server, Interactive WebAssembly and Interactive Auto.
evidence: To apply a render mode to a component use the `@rendermode` directive

question: How do I make an input update its bound field on every keystroke instead of when it loses focus?
expected_answer: Bind with @bind:event="oninput", for example <input @bind="searchText" @bind:event="oninput" />.
evidence: @bind:event="oninput"

question: How do I prevent the default browser action for an event in Blazor?
expected_answer: Use the @on{DOM EVENT}:preventDefault directive attribute, for example @onkeydown:preventDefault.
evidence: directive attribute to prevent the default action for an event

question: How does a component receive a cascading value?
expected_answer: By declaring a property with the [CascadingParameter] attribute. The value is provided by an ancestor CascadingValue component or registered at the root with AddCascadingValue.
evidence: [CascadingParameter]

question: When does Blazor dispose a component that implements IDisposable or IAsyncDisposable?
expected_answer: The framework calls for resource disposal when the component is removed from the UI.
evidence: the framework calls for resource disposal when the component is removed from the UI

question: How do I give a component its own styles that don't affect other components?
expected_answer: Use CSS isolation: create a .razor.css file with the same name as the component's .razor file, in the same folder. It is a scoped CSS file.
evidence: create a `.razor.css` file matching the name of the `.razor` file

question: My page renders a list of 10,000 items and it's slow. Which built-in feature helps?
expected_answer: Virtualization with the Virtualize component, which limits rendering to just the items that are currently visible.
evidence: Virtualization is a technique for limiting UI rendering to just the parts that are currently visible

question: What is the recommended way to validate a Blazor form?
expected_answer: Add data annotations validation attributes to the model and place a DataAnnotationsValidator component inside the EditForm.
evidence: place a DataAnnotationsValidator component in the EditForm

question: How do I call a JavaScript function from C# in a Blazor component?
expected_answer: Inject IJSRuntime and call InvokeAsync (or InvokeVoidAsync when no result is needed). The function identifier is relative to the global window scope.
evidence: inject the IJSRuntime abstraction

question: How do I call a static .NET method from JavaScript?
expected_answer: Call DotNet.invokeMethodAsync (recommended; DotNet.invokeMethod is synchronous and client-side only). The .NET method must be public, static and marked with [JSInvokable].
evidence: The .NET method must be public, static, and have the

question: A timer in my component updates a field, but the UI doesn't refresh correctly. How do I update the component from an external event?
expected_answer: Use InvokeAsync, which dispatches the code to Blazor's synchronization context, and call StateHasChanged inside it to rerender.
evidence: use the `InvokeAsync` method, which dispatches code execution to Blazor's synchronization context

question: How do I apply a filter to all controllers globally?
expected_answer: Add it to the Filters collection when registering MVC in Program.cs, for example builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews(options => options.Filters.Add<MyGlobalActionFilter>()).
evidence: options.Filters.Add<MyGlobalActionFilter>()

question: Which filter type runs first in the MVC filter pipeline?
expected_answer: Authorization filters. They determine whether the user is authorized and short-circuit the pipeline if not.
evidence: Determine whether the user is authorized for the request

question: When does an exception filter run, relative to model binding and the action result?
expected_answer: Exception filters run after model binding and action filters, but before the action result is executed. They handle unhandled exceptions that occur before the response body is written.
evidence: Run after model binding and action filters, but before the action result is executed

question: Where does model binding get its data from?
expected_answer: From sources such as route data, form fields and query strings. It converts the string data to .NET types and provides it to action parameters and public properties.
evidence: Retrieves data from various sources such as route data, form fields, and query strings

question: Do Web API controllers have to check ModelState.IsValid?
expected_answer: Not if they have the [ApiController] attribute. Then an automatic HTTP 400 response with error details is returned when model state is invalid.
evidence: an automatic HTTP 400 response containing error details is returned

question: How can I check whether a username is already taken while the user is filling in the form?
expected_answer: Use the [Remote] attribute, which implements client-side validation that calls a method on the server.
evidence: implements client-side validation that requires calling a method on the server

question: How many model validation errors are collected before validation stops?
expected_answer: 200 by default. The limit is configurable in Program.cs.
evidence: Validation stops when the maximum number of errors is reached (200 by default)

question: How do I mark a controller as belonging to an area?
expected_answer: Apply the [Area("Area name")] attribute to the controller, and add an area route, for example with {area:...} in MapControllerRoute or with MapAreaControllerRoute.
evidence: Matches all controllers with the `[Area("Area name")]` attribute

question: How do I control which Tag Helpers are available in my views?

question: How do I render a partial view using a Tag Helper?
expected_answer: Use the Partial Tag Helper: <partial name="_PartialName" />.
evidence: <partial name="_PartialName" />

question: I need a reusable widget, like a shopping cart summary, that has its own logic and data. What should I use instead of a partial view?
expected_answer: A view component. View components are similar to partial views but much more powerful: they have their own Invoke/InvokeAsync logic and don't depend on model binding.
evidence: View components are similar to partial views, but they're much more powerful

question: How does ASP.NET Core recognise a class as a view component?
expected_answer: By deriving from ViewComponent, applying the [ViewComponent] attribute (or deriving from a class with it), or giving the class a name that ends with the suffix ViewComponent. It must be public, non-nested and non-abstract.
evidence: Creating a class where the name ends with the suffix `ViewComponent`

question: Which method must every layout call, and what does it do?
expected_answer: RenderBody. The content of the view is rendered wherever RenderBody is called.
evidence: By default, every layout must call `RenderBody`

question: How do I restrict a controller to users in the Administrator role?
expected_answer: Apply [Authorize(Roles = "Administrator")] to the controller. Multiple roles can be given as a comma-separated list.
evidence: [Authorize(Roles = "Administrator")]

question: How should I handle very large file uploads without loading the whole file into memory?
expected_answer: Use unbuffered streaming instead of buffered model binding with IFormFile, which reads the entire file and is meant for smaller files.
evidence: buffered model binding for smaller files and unbuffered streaming for larger files
